scope.full_target:
Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

hypotheses.statement: u:ℝ^n × (0,∞) → ℝ^m is jointly C^∞ (smooth) on this open domain.
For every x∈ℝ^n and every t>0, |u(x,t)|=1.
For every x∈ℝ^n and every t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of a selected scalar field is assumed.

binders.type: compact subset of ℝ^n, existentially bound

hypotheses.statement: For every pair of real times 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact C⊂ℝ^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and every r∈[s,t].

source.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is absolutely Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n, E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. In addition E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0; no assertion at time zero is made.

correspondence.explanation: Positive integer dimensions are represented by n,m : ℕ with H001 : 1≤n ∧ 1≤m, a bijective encoding. X n is the usual real Cartesian coordinate space with product Lebesgue measure; V m has exactly the Euclidean norm and dot product. Fin n reindexes all n coordinates without changing finite sums. H002 asserts joint C∞ smoothness on precisely t>0, using the inner infinity smoothness index; H003/H004 keep both unit conditions. H005 is the original pointwise existential scalar normality equation, with no scalar field regularity. H006 retains a single compact spatial set for every entire positive closed time interval. A source map on t>0 extends arbitrarily to the total u used here, and any such u restricts back; locality preserves all positive-time derivatives and hypotheses in both directions. dt, dx and lap give the componentwise time/spatial derivatives and Laplacian, and density is exactly the unhalved sum of their Euclidean squares. T004 proves the guard that makes energy the actual finite Lebesgue integral. The conclusion explicitly asserts absolute integrability, real differentiability and zero derivative at every positive time, together with energy equality for every pair of positive times. Restriction and extension therefore give the whole source target in both directions; no conclusion at nonpositive times or additional hypothesis is present.
